name: LongText-Bench
intro: LongText-Bench 是 X-Omni 提出的中英文长文字图像生成基准。论文 v1 附录 A 记录了八类场景、每类 20 条 GPT-4o 候选和逐条人工后审，共 160 条提示；固定公开版实际提供 160 条英文和 160 条中文记录，两文件共享 160 个非连续 ID 及类别/长短标签，但并非统一逐字翻译，中文构造路线未披露。每种语言的每个提示预期生成四张图；官方评测按 MODE 分语言运行，以 Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 做 OCR，按英文词或中文字符做无序 Counter 交集，并对全部已读入图像的标准单位做微平均 Text Score。
build_method: 八类场景各用 GPT-4o 生成短/长各 10 条提示，逐条人工后审并调节文字长度；固定发布版提供共享 ID 的中英文语言视图
metric: 分语言 Text Score = Σ匹配标准单位 / Σ标准单位（英文词、中文字符；无序 Counter 交集）；HF Avg = (英文 + 中文) / 2
modality: 文本提示, 生成图像
task_type: 图像生成, 长文字渲染, OCR评测
eval_feature: 每提示预期四图、分语言 MODE、Qwen OCR、无序多重集匹配、全图微平均
scale: 论文构建为 160 条提示；固定发布版为 160 个共享 ID / 320 条语言记录；每语言预期 640 张评测图，双语共 1,280 张
task_type_en: Image Generation, Long-text Rendering, OCR Evaluation
build_method_en: Eight scenarios with 10 short and 10 long GPT-4o prompts each, per-prompt manual post-review and text-length adjustment, followed by fixed English and Chinese release views sharing prompt IDs
eval_feature_en: Expected four images per prompt, per-language MODE, Qwen OCR, unordered multiset matching, and image-wide micro-aggregation
intro_en: LongText-Bench is the English-and-Chinese long-text image-generation benchmark introduced by X-Omni. Paper v1 Appendix A documents eight scenarios, 20 GPT-4o candidates per scenario, and per-prompt manual post-review, yielding 160 prompts. The fixed public release instead exposes 160 English and 160 Chinese records that share 160 non-contiguous IDs plus category and short/long labels; they are not uniform literal translations, and the Chinese construction route is undisclosed. Four images are expected for every prompt in each language. Official evaluation runs one language MODE at a time, applies Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct OCR, intersects unordered English-word or Chinese-character Counters, and micro-averages matched ground-truth units over every ingested image.
scale_en: Paper construction: 160 prompts; fixed release: 160 shared IDs / 320 language records; expected 640 evaluation images per language and 1,280 across both
metric_en: Per-language Text Score = sum of matched ground-truth units / sum of ground-truth units (English words or Chinese characters; unordered Counter intersection); HF Avg = (English + Chinese) / 2

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against the only current arXiv version, arXiv:2507.22058v1 (Appendix A, Figure 7, and Table 1), official repository commit 2b8237bb3789638c290eeda3e83ed81bd3652c3b, and Hugging Face dataset revision 429e30e9c1e0dea535038ae4238ea6ec42823098. The two prompt files at those code and data revisions are byte-identical: English SHA-256 a2130769e72bd8560470a066114cdac87f80f1eb071ba6bc0f7033225a9be0d8 and Chinese SHA-256 6512cd121ac093e8113e114d76eb2c0ce967c220b18e2049e1063554ce496758. The paper defines eight text-rich scenarios—signboards, labeled objects, printed materials, web pages, slides, posters, captions, and dialogues—then asks GPT-4o for 20 image-generation prompts per scenario, 10 short and 10 long, followed by manual review of every prompt and rendered-text length adjustment for a balanced distribution, yielding 160 prompts. The exact GPT-4o prompt, snapshot, decoding configuration, source corpus, annotator count, rejection criteria, adjudication, and any additional filter or QC protocol are not disclosed. The paper also does not explain how the Chinese records are derived. The fixed release contains 160 English and 160 Chinese rows with the same 160 prompt IDs, categories, and short/long labels; fields are category, length, prompt, text, text_length, and prompt_id. IDs occupy 0–79, 100–139, and 160–199, with no train/dev/test split. The two language views are not uniform literal translations: for example, corresponding records can omit rendered-text segments, and 15 of 160 ID pairs have different text-array lengths. Paper length statements are distributions, not hard filters. In the fixed files, English short rows span text_length 10–33 and long rows 14–66, while Chinese short rows span 14–61 and long rows 26–111. Candidate generation is expected to produce four PNGs per prompt and language, named prompt_id_repeat_id.png, but the paper and evaluator do not standardize candidate model/checkpoint, prompt rewriting or truncation, resolution, seed, sampler, guidance, or safety-rejection handling. The evaluator merely sorts every PNG in the chosen folder, parses the integer before an underscore (or before the extension), maps it through the MODE-selected prompt file, and does not enforce prompt coverage, four repeats, or a complete 640-image language run. It loads Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct by model name without a revision pin, in BF16, feeds the image plus a fixed English OCR instruction whose empty-case reply is exactly "No text recognized" without a trailing period, and generates at most 1,024 new tokens without an explicit input-truncation flag. The README pins Transformers 4.52.0. The cleanup helper lists addCriterion and "No text recognized." with a trailing period, but each loop iteration restarts from the original OCR string. The first addCriterion removal is therefore overwritten, and only the second, period-suffixed replacement can survive; when the model follows the prompt exactly and returns the no-period empty phrase, that output is not cleared at all. Scoring joins the ground-truth text segments, removes punctuation, lowercases and whitespace-normalizes English before word splitting, or removes spacing and uses each retained Chinese/Latin/digit character in Chinese mode. Counter intersection caps duplicate matches at the smaller multiplicity, discards segment and relative order, and does not penalize extra OCR units. The per-image field text_accuray is a misspelled recall-like matched-ground-truth ratio; the reported Text Score is sum of matched units divided by sum of ground-truth units across all ingested images, not a mean over prompts or four repeats. One run reports one language to four decimals. The pinned HF card publishes a static table of 11 model rows with English, Chinese, and their arithmetic-mean Avg; there is no human upper bound, submission protocol, or live evaluation service. Code and prompt data are public under Apache-2.0, but no official generated-image bundle is released. Finally, the pinned eval.sh concatenates results.jsonl but calls summary_scores.py on nonexistent results.json, so the wrapper requires a filename correction before end-to-end execution.
